page: Amazon Web Services i3.metal is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server provisioned with dedicated physical hardware. It operates on two Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors featuring an x86_64 architecture, providing 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The platform is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering 7.11 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture is anchored by 15,200 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local capacity, while networking capabilities provide a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. Single-core tests reflect the limitations of the older Broadwell microarchitecture, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 992.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating in the bottom 10%. Conversely, aggregate multi-core and throughput performance sits firmly in the middle 50% across most metrics, recording a PassMark CPU score of 40,174.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,899.0. Memory bandwidth remains solid with 121.2 GB/sec on uncached large reads, allowing Redis SET operations to reach 45.69 million operations per second and PassMark database operations to benchmark at 18,590.76.

From an architectural standpoint, i3.metal trades modern per-core processing efficiency and instruction sets like AVX-512 for substantial NVMe density and bare-metal hypervisor bypass. This profile makes it cost-efficient for heavy I/O systems requiring direct hardware access, low-latency disk access, and large RAM footprints, whereas compute-bound jobs with low storage demands would find the older CPU cores inefficient.

Workloads best aligned with i3.metal include high-transaction NoSQL and relational database engines, distributed data stores like Apache Cassandra or Elasticsearch, in-memory caching layers with persistence, and custom bare-metal virtualization platforms requiring direct access to physical CPU and NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.metal is a bare-metal storage-optimized server powered by 36-core Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processors delivering 72 vCPUs at 2.3 GHz. It includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and 15,200 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage, operating without dedicated graphics acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show modest single-thread CPU performance consistent with its legacy Broadwell architecture, alongside average multi-core and throughput metrics such as a PassMark CPU score of 40,174.7 and 45.69 million Redis SET operations per second. The server trades cutting-edge compute efficiency for dense local high-speed storage and bare-metal execution without hypervisor overhead. Consequently, i3.metal fits high-throughput transactional databases, large-scale distributed file systems, Elasticsearch clusters, and enterprise virtualization platforms requiring direct low-latency access to expansive NVMe storage.
